messages.content: "Can you help me plan a trip? I need to know the distance in kilometers from New York to London using the 'geodistance.find' function, then I want to know the time difference between New York and London using the 'timezones.get_difference' function. After that, I want to find flights from New York to London on the date of 'next friday' using the 'flights.search' function. Finally, I want to know the distance in miles from London to Paris using the 'geodistance.find' function again."

function.description: Find the time difference between two cities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.description: Find the distance between two cities on the globe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Also they mention 'timezones.get_difference' which is timezones_get_difference. And 'flights.search' which is flights_search.

We can do them one after another. The system expects us to output a function call. But we can only output one function call at a time. So we need to decide which function to call first. The user wants the distance first. So we call geodistance_find with origin=New York, destination=London, unit=kilometers. Then we will get response. Then we call timezones_get_difference. Then flights_search. Then geodistance_find again.

But we can't output multiple calls in one message. We need to output one function call, wait for the tool to return, then output next. So we need to start with geodistance_find. We'll call it with unit="kilometers". Then we will get result. Then we will call timezones_get_difference. Then flights_search. Then geodistance_find again with unit="miles".
